entry.title: Texas nipple cactus (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that according to one cacti nurseryman, the Texas nipple cactus (pictured) is so easy to grow that connoisseurs almost look down on it?

entry.title: Thomas Burdet (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Thomas Burdet supposedly plotted treason against King Edward IV in 1477 after he killed Burdet's favourite white deer?

entry.title: Malibu Feed Bin (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that 23 tons of dog food were once stolen from the Malibu Feed Bin?

entry.title: Alf Jacques (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Alf Jacques crafted more than 80,000 wooden lacrosse sticks in his lifetime?

entry.title: Lustrous Pearls (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the Chinese silent film Lustrous Pearls has been described as blurring the differences between male and female bodies through long shots?

entry.title: Rosalind "Sister Roz" Gefre (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that by 2006, Catholic sister Rosalind "Sister Roz" Gefre has given an estimated 7,000 massages at St. Paul Saints baseball games?

entry.title: Inky the octopus (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Inky the octopus attracted worldwide media attention after escaping from the National Aquarium of New Zealand?

entry.title: Brother Justus (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Benedictine monk Brother Justus helped make stills so that farmers could illegally make alcohol during the Prohibition?
